name: Wörgl
kurzbeschreibung: The gateway to the Kitzbüheler Alpen – a vibrant district capital with modern infrastructure and a historic old town.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The city of Wörgl is situated at 511 metres above sea level in the lower Inn Valley within the Tyrolean district of Kufstein, right where the Brixentaler Ache flows into the River Inn. With approximately 14,450 residents, Wörgl is the second-largest city in the district and the thriving commercial, transport, and economic powerhouse of the Tyrolean lowlands. Set in a wide valley basin between the Northern Limestone Alps and the Kitzbühel Alps, this lively shopping city blends urban energy with immediate access to mountain recreation. Wörgl serves as a pivotal gateway connecting the Inn Valley, the Brixental towards Kitzbühel, and the high valley of Wildschönau.

Geschichte

Archaeological finds in Egerndörfl indicate settlements dating back to the Bronze Age Urnfield culture and the Roman era. The town was first documented in 1120 with the mention of Heinrich de Uuergile. Emperor Franz Joseph I granted Wörgl market status in 1911, and it achieved full city status in 1951. Wörgl gained international renown in 1932–1933 through the revolutionary Wörgl Freigeld experiment: during the Great Depression, Mayor Michael Unterguggenberger introduced stamp scrip based on Silvio Gesell's economic theories. This local currency, which depreciated slightly each month, dramatically stimulated the local economy, eliminated unemployment, and became famous worldwide as the Miracle of Wörgl. The parish church of St. Lawrence, dating back to 1212, was rebuilt in classical style after an 1836 fire.

Anreise

Wörgl benefits from superb transport connections in western Austria. Drivers access the city directly via the Inntal motorway A12 using junctions Wörgl West and Wörgl Ost, as well as the federal road B171. The Brixentalstraße B170 branches off here towards Kitzbühel. Wörgl Hauptbahnhof is one of Austria's premier railway junctions, connecting the Westbahn, Giselabahn towards Salzburg, and the international Brenner transit corridor. Frequent Railjet, ICE, Eurocity, and Nightjet trains stop here. Locally, a comprehensive city bus system serves all urban quarters, alongside regional buses into adjacent valleys.

Tipps

Wörgl's Bahnhofstraße is celebrated as the second-longest shopping street in Tyrol, featuring a pedestrian-friendly promenade with boutiques, traditional inns, and pavement cafés. On the city outskirts, the modern M4 shopping and entertainment complex provides retail stores, restaurants, and a multiplex cinema. Cultural visitors should explore the Wörgl City Museum, which presents archaeological treasures and an extensive permanent exhibition on the historic 1932 Freigeld monetary experiment. For outdoor adventures, hiking up to the local Möslalm alpine pasture provides rewarding views over the Inn Valley and excellent mountain biking routes.
